SUMMARY: Epic 24 - Code review findings (2026-10-06)
DESCRIPTION: The 28 findings of the 2026-10-06 code review of commit 776b69be (docs/reviews/code-review-2026-10-06.csv and .md), one ticket per finding: LED-(293+n) is REV-00n. Ranked by risk: tenant isolation and atomic money first, then offline write protection, the durable queue, money correctness, the read/cache lifecycle, and verification, types and performance. Build order: epic-24-build-order.md.

SUMMARY: Loan calculations answer only for the owner of the purchase
USER_STORY: As a user, I want my loan amounts readable only by me, so another account cannot learn what I owe.
DESCRIPTION: loan_purchase_paid_amount and loan_purchase_due_amount are SECURITY DEFINER functions in the exposed public schema. They filter only by purchase UUID. No migration revokes their execution or checks auth.uid(). Impact: A caller with a known purchase UUID can request its paid or due amount outside the owner's RLS policy. Exploit requires a valid UUID. Hosted grants were not inspected. (REV-001; supabase/migrations/20260810123000_add_financed_purchases.sql:117; supabase/migrations/20260810130000_add_loan_opening_progress.sql:45; supabase/config.toml:13). Fix: Add a migration that makes API-facing calculations SECURITY INVOKER with RLS, or moves privileged helpers into an unexposed private schema. Revoke EXECUTE explicitly from PUBLIC and anon, and grant only intended roles. Require ownership in any exposed definer wrapper. Owner decision in /plan: (A) SECURITY INVOKER with RLS, or (B) move the helpers to an unexposed private schema behind owner-checked wrappers. Either way the SECURITY INVOKER add_unitemised_purchase (20260925110100:43) and the definer triggers in 20261006130000 must keep working; the client never calls these functions directly.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Run SQL/API tests as anon and user B against user A's seeded purchase. Neither role should receive its financial values. Verify owner calls and allocation triggers still work; (b) SQL check inside begin .. rollback (anon, owner and a second user) recorded in the retro; (c) migration applies cleanly to an empty database in CI; (d) existing loan allocation and unitemised purchase flows unchanged.

SUMMARY: A profile read from a previous session never reappears after sign-out
USER_STORY: As a user, I want signing out or switching accounts to leave none of the previous account's profile on screen or in this browser.
DESCRIPTION: fetchProfile guards pending-setting reconciliation by userIdRef, but unconditionally calls setProfile and writeCache after the request. The auth callback clears profile only for no session, and does not clear it when the user changes. Impact: A response started as user A can arrive after sign-out or a switch to B, repopulating A's browser cache and displaying the wrong profile. Applying B's pending settings to A's result is also possible. (REV-002; src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:243; src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:269; src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:303). Fix: Track an auth/request generation and check it before every state update, cache write and migration side effect. Clear profile immediately on user changes. Cancel or discard outstanding reads when signing out.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Delay A's profile response, sign out or switch to B, then release it. Assert no A data is displayed or recreated in browser storage; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib (auth/request generation guard); (c) sign-out still clears the personal copies listed by LED-268.

SUMMARY: Card payment tracking is recorded once and atomically
USER_STORY: As a user, I want every card payment counted exactly once on its statement, even with two payments at once or a dropped connection.
DESCRIPTION: The transfer, payment-history insert, statement read and absolute statement update are separate requests. createWithStatement launches tracking without awaiting it. Synced callbacks also launch tracking without awaiting completion. Impact: Closing the app after the transfer can permanently miss statement tracking. Two payments can read the same statement_paid_amount and overwrite one another's increment. Queued payments to the same card can run their follow-ups concurrently. (REV-003; src/hooks/useCardPayment.ts:51; src/hooks/useCardPayment.ts:66; src/hooks/useCardPayment.ts:94; src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx:235). Fix: Move transfer creation, unique payment linkage and statement updates into one idempotent SECURITY INVOKER RPC or database trigger. Lock the card row and update the paid amount atomically. Use the same operation for manual, imported and recurring payments. One idempotent SECURITY INVOKER RPC (or trigger) for transfer, payment link and statement update, used by manual, imported, recurring (generateDueRecurring) and synced (recordSynced) payments.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Save two payments concurrently and verify both are counted exactly once. Simulate a lost response and replay the same transaction ID. Verify rollback when an intermediate step fails; (b) SQL check inside begin .. rollback (anon, owner and a second user) recorded in the retro; (c) migration applies cleanly to an empty database in CI; (d) the Fix notification remains only for genuine failures.

SUMMARY: A queued edit never silently overwrites a newer server edit
USER_STORY: As a user, I want an edit I made offline to stop and ask, not overwrite a newer change made on another device.
DESCRIPTION: A failed conflict read returns unknown and the write proceeds. The comparison uses the client enqueue timestamp rather than the revision originally read. The check and write are separate requests with no revision condition. Impact: Remote changes made after a cached read but before enqueue are overwritten. Failed checks, clock skew and writes between SELECT and UPDATE/DELETE also allow lost updates. (REV-004; src/lib/queueDrain.ts:82; src/lib/queueDrain.ts:102; src/lib/queueDrain.ts:124; src/lib/queueState.ts:13). Fix: Capture the original server revision in each queued mutation. Apply a conditional update/delete against that revision in one server operation. Retain the item when verification fails and surface a retryable error. Reserve bypass for an explicit Keep mine choice.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Cover failed SELECT, stale cached revisions, skewed client clocks and a concurrent write between read and mutation. Each case must retain or flag the mutation instead of silently overwriting; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib (queueDrain/queueState); (c) Keep mine remains the only explicit bypass.

SUMMARY: Imported offline transactions keep their IDs through sync
USER_STORY: As a user, I want to edit or delete a transaction I imported offline before it syncs, and have that change apply to the same row.
DESCRIPTION: bulkCreateTransactions assigns UUIDs to optimistic rows, then queues the original values through enqueueInsert(values) without those UUIDs. The database generates different IDs on replay. Impact: Edits and deletes before sync target nonexistent IDs. Lost responses or concurrent drains can insert duplicate financial transactions. Offline imported card payments also have no transaction ID for their payment-history linkage. (REV-005; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:373; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:381; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:183). Fix: Generate one ID per imported row and reuse it in the optimistic transaction, queued insert and all follow-up writes. Make replay idempotent by reconciling an existing ID and its owner/payload rather than treating every duplicate-key response as a new failure.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Import offline, edit and delete rows before syncing, and assert the same IDs reach the server. Replay after a simulated committed insert with a lost response and verify no duplicate or permanently failed item; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib; (c) offline imported card payments carry their transaction ID to payment tracking (LED-296).

SUMMARY: An edit made while a queued insert is saving is not lost
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a change I make to a pending transaction while it syncs to reach the server, not be dropped.
DESCRIPTION: The drain snapshots queued payloads. editQueuedInsert can modify the stored item while a request is in flight. mergeDrainResult removes a successfully sent ID without checking whether its stored payload changed. Impact: The old payload is saved and the newer local edit is removed from the queue even though it was never sent. (REV-006; src/lib/queueDrain.ts:171; src/lib/queueDrain.ts:207; src/lib/queueState.ts:180). Fix: Version queued items and acknowledge only the version actually sent. Preserve a newer version as an update after the insert succeeds, or prevent editing the item while in flight with a clear UI state. Owner decision in /plan: (A) version queue items and acknowledge only the version sent, or (B) lock editing while the row is saving, with a clear state.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Pause an insert, change its amount in the queue, then complete the original request. Verify the newer amount is still queued and eventually reaches the database; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib (mergeDrainResult).

SUMMARY: A receipt attached offline or after a failed upload still uploads
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a receipt I attach to an existing transaction to upload when it can, instead of being saved as a broken link.
DESCRIPTION: isPendingReceipt requires operation === insert. Offline edits can queue a pending-receipt marker in an update. An online upload failure can return the same marker while the transaction saves through the online path, with no receipt job queued. Impact: The transaction can report success with an attachment that never uploads. resolveReceiptUrl explicitly cannot display pending markers. (REV-007; src/lib/queueDrain.ts:53; src/hooks/useReceiptAttachment.ts:136; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:217). Fix: Represent attachment upload as a durable job independent of insert/update mode. Resolve pending files for both operations, and enqueue recovery when an online upload falls back to local storage. Do not store an unresolved marker as a completed server attachment.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Attach a receipt to an existing transaction offline and simulate an upload failure while online. Reconnect and verify the stored path resolves to the uploaded file; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib.

SUMMARY: A receipt uploaded before a failed save stays attached
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a receipt that already uploaded to stay attached when the save is retried.
DESCRIPTION: resolveReceipt removes the local blob immediately after upload and returns a changed payload only in memory. If the insert throws, the catch retains the original item with its pending marker. The next replay finds no blob and replaces receipt_url with null. Impact: A successfully uploaded file becomes orphaned and the transaction loses its receipt after retry. (REV-008; src/lib/queueDrain.ts:78; src/lib/queueDrain.ts:109; src/lib/queueDrain.ts:198). Fix: Persist the resolved storage path before attempting the row mutation. Retain the local blob until that path is durably recorded. Preserve the resolved payload on thrown errors and add cleanup for abandoned uploads.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Upload successfully, throw before the row insert completes, reload and retry. Verify the receipt remains attached and no extra file is uploaded; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib (resolveReceipt retry path).

SUMMARY: Two open tabs share one queue without losing or doubling writes
USER_STORY: As a user with the app open in two tabs, I want every offline change saved once, whichever tab syncs it.
DESCRIPTION: enqueue performs a localStorage read-modify-write. singleFlight and listener sets exist only within one JavaScript module instance. There is no storage-event handler, Web Lock or transactional shared queue. Impact: Two tabs can overwrite each other's enqueues or drain the same items concurrently. A duplicate insert may be reported as failed even when another tab already saved it. (REV-009; src/lib/offlineQueue.ts:17; src/lib/offlineQueue.ts:43; src/lib/offlineQueue.ts:54; src/lib/queueDrain.ts:229). Fix: Use a transactional IndexedDB queue and coordinate drains across tabs with Web Locks or a persisted lease. Broadcast queue changes. Keep database writes idempotent because a browser lock alone cannot guarantee exactly-once delivery.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Enqueue and reconnect from two browser contexts at the same time. Verify all items remain visible, every mutation applies once and both tabs converge; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib where the coordination logic allows; (c) manual two-context check recorded in the retro.

SUMMARY: An offline save shows success only once it is stored
USER_STORY: As a user, I want an offline save to say it failed when this browser could not store it, instead of showing a balance that disappears on reload.
DESCRIPTION: Offline creates update transaction state and cached account balances before enqueueInsert. Queue writes can throw on quota/storage errors, while cache writes silently skip those errors. Impact: The UI can show a transaction and changed balance even when no recoverable sync item exists. Reload can then lose the apparent save. (REV-010; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:209; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:213; src/lib/offlineQueue.ts:43; src/lib/dataCache.ts:25). Fix: Persist the queued mutation before announcing or applying optimistic success. Return a structured storage error and roll back any optimistic state if persistence fails. Use IndexedDB and report unavailable durable storage. Owner decision in /plan: move the queue from localStorage to IndexedDB here (LED-302 and LED-318 build on it), with a one-time move of any existing localStorage queue.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Make localStorage.setItem throw a quota error. Assert the save reports failure, displayed balances remain correct and no phantom transaction appears; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib; (c) existing queued items survive the storage move.

SUMMARY: Changing filters quickly shows only the latest results
USER_STORY: As a user, I want the transactions on screen to always match the filters I chose last.
DESCRIPTION: fetch commits rows and loading/error state unconditionally after awaiting the request. Changing filters starts a new fetch without a request-generation check or cancellation. dedupeAsync shares equal keys but does not prevent results from older keys being committed. Impact: Changing account/category/date filters quickly can display rows from the previous filter under the current controls, or clear the new request's loading state prematurely. (REV-011; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:87; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:134; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:145; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:151). Fix: Associate displayed data with its query key. Discard responses whose request generation/key is no longer current, and pass cancellation checks into readAllPages. Reuse a small tested request-state abstraction across affected hooks.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Delay filter A, complete filter B, then release A. Assert only B rows and B errors/loading state remain; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib (request-state abstraction).

SUMMARY: Pending transactions sync when the app opens online
USER_STORY: As a user, I want what I saved offline to sync as soon as I reopen the app with a connection.
DESCRIPTION: Automatic sync is attached to the window online event. The provider does not call syncNow when it mounts with navigator.onLine already true, and queue subscriptions only refresh counts. Impact: Transactions saved offline can remain pending after the user closes the app and reopens it with a working connection. No online transition occurs to trigger replay. (REV-012; src/contexts/NetworkStatusContext.tsx:40; src/contexts/NetworkStatusContext.tsx:110). Fix: Drain on authenticated startup when online and pending items exist. Schedule a bounded retry for transient failures and check readiness on focus/visibility changes. Coordinate startup with registration of durable follow-ups.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Seed a pending item, start the app already online and verify it syncs without clicking Sync or toggling connectivity; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib where the readiness rule allows; (c) no second drain runs alongside another tab (LED-302).

SUMMARY: Every mounted list and total refreshes after a change
USER_STORY: As a user, I want balances, totals and lists on screen to update after any save or sync, without navigating away.
DESCRIPTION: Account listeners only reload the cached accounts. useAccounts does not subscribe to post-drain sync notifications. Online transaction fetches do not refresh account caches. Transaction notifications reload each hook's own filter-specific cache rather than invalidating related keys. Impact: Mounted account balances, Home totals or transaction lists can remain stale after online mutations, queue resolution or a mutation through another filtered hook. Cache events can simply reload the same outdated data. (REV-013; src/hooks/useAccounts.ts:60; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:72; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:225; src/hooks/useNetworkStatus.ts:29). Fix: Introduce a shared entity/query store with explicit invalidation for transactions, accounts, budgets, goals and card payments. Invalidate or reconcile all affected keys after server writes and queue drain. Reuse one subscription contract instead of cache-only refresh events.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Keep Home/layout and a filtered list mounted. Create, edit, discard and sync transactions through another surface. Verify all lists, balances and dependent totals converge without navigation; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib (invalidation map).

SUMMARY: A list opened offline without a copy says so instead of loading forever
USER_STORY: As a user offline, I want a list this device has no copy of to tell me so and retry when I am back online.
DESCRIPTION: When no cache is found these hooks set loading true and immediately return on navigator.onLine === false without setting an offline error or clearing loading. The same pattern occurs in several cached data hooks. Impact: A new filter or an expired/cleared cache produces an indefinite skeleton with no useful explanation or recovery state. (REV-014; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:98; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:106; src/hooks/useAccounts.ts:26; src/hooks/useAccounts.ts:34). Fix: Resolve offline-without-cache as an explicit unavailable state through resolveLoadState. Clear loading, name the missing offline data and retry when connectivity returns. Share this policy across list hooks. Resolve through resolveLoadState (AGENTS.md: a failed read is never rendered as an empty state).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Open an uncached account/filter while offline, and repeat with a cache older than its TTL. Assert an actionable offline state replaces loading; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib; (c) copy matches the LED-53 offline-state wording.

SUMMARY: History and export reads include every row past 1000
USER_STORY: As a user with a long history, I want lists and exports to include all my records.
DESCRIPTION: Credit-card payment history, loan purchases and all-subcategory reads have no pagination. The configured PostgREST cap is 1000 rows. ExportDataCard uses these hooks as complete export sources. Impact: Larger histories and exports omit records without an error. Missing loan purchases also omit their allocations and understate schedules. (REV-015; src/hooks/useCreditCardPayments.ts:34; src/hooks/useLoanPurchases.ts:45; src/hooks/useSubcategories.ts:130; supabase/config.toml:18). Fix: Use readAllPages with a deterministic total order for every potentially unbounded source, including these export reads. Batch large ID filters or replace them with joined server queries when URLs become too large.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Seed more than 1000 payment, purchase and subcategory rows. Verify reads and CSV exports include all IDs exactly once; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib where batching logic is added.

SUMMARY: The account export includes archived accounts
USER_STORY: As a user exporting my data, I want archived accounts in the file so retained transactions keep their context.
DESCRIPTION: The shared useAccounts hook always filters is_active = true. SignedInExport reuses it for the full account export, although archived loans/accounts remain in the database and can retain transaction history. Impact: A user exporting before deletion loses archived account records and the account context needed to interpret their retained transactions. (REV-016; src/hooks/useAccounts.ts:40; src/components/legal/ExportDataCard.tsx:90; src/components/legal/ExportDataCard.tsx:128). Fix: Add an explicit includeArchived/export read mode or a dedicated complete account query, preserving the active-only behavior for normal account pickers. Keep the export dataset separate from display-only filtering.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Archive an account with retained history, export, and verify its row is present with Active = no and correct balances/metadata; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib (dataExport); (c) account pickers still show active accounts only.

SUMMARY: The cash-flow forecast converts each amount to the base currency
USER_STORY: As a user with accounts in several currencies, I want the forecast to add amounts in one currency.
DESCRIPTION: buildCashFlowForecast sums occurrences * tx.amount without receiving a rate table or target currency. Its starting balance is stats.totalBalance, already converted. The card labels all forecast amounts using the base currency. Impact: A USD recurring amount can be treated as the same number of PHP or EUR, producing incorrect projected income, expenses and closing balance. (REV-017; src/hooks/useDashboardData.ts:234; src/hooks/useDashboardData.ts:260; src/components/dashboard/DashboardCashFlowForecastCard.tsx:126). Fix: Move the forecast calculation to a pure src/lib helper and convert each occurrence into the base currency with amountInCurrency/sumConverted. Exclude and identify currencies lacking rates, including item totals and sort order. The forecast moves to a pure src/lib helper using amountInCurrency / sumConverted; currencies without a rate are excluded and named (LED-03 pattern).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Test a PHP balance with USD income and EUR expenses, same-currency rows and missing rates. Compare projected balances to independently converted amounts; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib.

SUMMARY: Savings-goal contributions convert to the goal currency
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a goal's contributed total to be in the goal's currency, with any unrated currency named.
DESCRIPTION: totalContributed directly sums linked transaction amounts, subtracting expenses, without converting transaction.currency into goal.currency. The goal card formats that sum in the goal's currency. Impact: Cross-currency linked transactions produce misleading contribution totals. (REV-018; src/hooks/useSavingsGoals.ts:79; src/pages/BudgetsPage.tsx:1141). Fix: Calculate contributions in the goal currency using the shared conversion helper. Keep missing-rate currencies visible and exclude them from the numeric total until a rate is available.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Link USD and PHP transactions to a PHP goal and verify the total at a known rate. Verify a missing rate is named rather than counted one-to-one; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib.

SUMMARY: Concurrent savings contributions are all counted
USER_STORY: As a user adding to a goal from two devices, I want both contributions counted exactly once.
DESCRIPTION: addContribution calls updateGoal with current_amount = currentAmount + amount, where currentAmount comes from the rendered goal snapshot. Impact: Two devices contributing to the same goal can read the same starting value and lose one contribution when their absolute updates overwrite each other. (REV-019; src/hooks/useSavingsGoals.ts:121; src/pages/BudgetsPage.tsx:1254). Fix: Add a SECURITY INVOKER RPC that locks the owned goal and increments current_amount in SQL. Give each contribution a unique operation ID for safe retries or record contributions as ledger rows. Owner decision in /plan: (A) SECURITY INVOKER RPC that increments current_amount with an operation ID, or (B) record contributions as ledger rows.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Starting at 100, concurrently add 20 and 30 and assert the result is 150. Replay an operation after a lost response and assert it is counted once; (b) SQL check inside begin .. rollback (anon, owner and a second user) recorded in the retro; (c) migration applies cleanly to an empty database in CI.

SUMMARY: A failed contribution keeps the dialog open and says why
USER_STORY: As a user, I want to know when a contribution did not save, and keep what I typed to retry.
DESCRIPTION: handleContribution awaits addContribution but ignores the returned MutationResult, then unconditionally clears contributionGoal. The hook returns errors for offline and rejected writes. Impact: The user can believe a contribution saved when it was rejected or never sent. (REV-020; src/pages/BudgetsPage.tsx:1252). Fix: Check error and errorDetail before closing the contribution dialog. Preserve the input and display a FormError or notification with a retry action, following the adjacent create/edit goal handlers. Follow the adjacent create/edit goal handlers and FormError (LED-55).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Attempt a contribution offline and simulate a denied database write. Assert the dialog stays open and a clear error appears without changing the saved amount; (b) offline and denied-write cases checked in the retro.

SUMMARY: Every user-owned reference is checked for ownership
USER_STORY: As a user, I want no other account able to link its records to mine.
DESCRIPTION: The transaction ownership trigger covers accounts, categories and subcategories but not the subsequently added goal_id. Transaction rules lack a category ownership check. Credit-card payment rows lack ownership checks for account_id and transaction_id. Their RLS checks only the row's user_id. Impact: A caller knowing another user's UUID can create cross-owner relationships. Foreign-key checks bypass RLS, so RLS on the referenced table does not enforce this invariant. This is not evidence of unrestricted reads of those rows. (REV-021; supabase/migrations/20260507160000_baseline_schema.sql:285; supabase/migrations/20260507160000_baseline_schema.sql:592; supabase/migrations/20260507160000_baseline_schema.sql:612; supabase/migrations/20261001100000_card_payment_follows_its_transfer.sql:17). Fix: Add composite owner-scoped foreign keys or ownership triggers for every user-owned reference. Validate a payment's transaction, destination and amount relationship as well as its owner. Backfill or repair invalid links before validating constraints. Backfill or repair invalid links before validating constraints; the repair query and its row count go in the retro.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) As user B, attempt to reference A's goal, rule category, account and transfer. Each write must fail. Owner-consistent writes must succeed; (b) SQL check inside begin .. rollback (anon, owner and a second user) recorded in the retro; (c) migration applies cleanly to an empty database in CI; (d) owner-consistent writes, including card payment follow-ups (20261001100000), still succeed.

SUMMARY: Changing category never leaves a subcategory from another category
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a transaction moved to a new category to drop or remap a subcategory that no longer fits.
DESCRIPTION: bulkUpdateCategory changes category_id only. The ownership trigger checks that subcategory_id belongs to the same user but does not require subcategories.category_id = transactions.category_id. Impact: A transaction moved from Food to Travel can retain a Food subcategory, giving inconsistent filters, exports and category reports. (REV-022; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:334; supabase/migrations/20260507160000_baseline_schema.sql:308). Fix: Clear subcategory_id when changing the parent category unless an explicit mapping preserves it. Add a database guard requiring the selected subcategory to belong to the selected category, including subcategory reparenting paths. Owner decision in /plan: clear subcategory_id on parent change, or remap through an explicit mapping. Add a database guard either way.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Bulk-change a categorized transaction with a subcategory and assert the child is cleared or remapped. Attempt a mismatched parent/child insert directly and verify it is rejected; (b) SQL check inside begin .. rollback (anon, owner and a second user) recorded in the retro; (c) migration applies cleanly to an empty database in CI; (d) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib for any client-side mapping.

SUMMARY: An account with history cannot silently change currency
USER_STORY: As a user, I want my balances never to mix currencies because an account currency was edited.
DESCRIPTION: The edit form exposes the currency selector and updateAccountWithAdjustment writes changed metadata. There is no server guard or history conversion when an account currency changes. Existing transaction amounts/currencies and stored balance are retained. Impact: Changing a populated USD account to PHP relabels its balance while old transaction deltas still use the old units. Subsequent edits/deletes mix units in the same balance. (REV-023; src/components/accounts/AccountForm.tsx:163; src/hooks/useAccounts.ts:113; supabase/migrations/20260507160000_baseline_schema.sql:105). Fix: Prevent currency changes once transaction or financed-purchase history exists, in both the form and the database. If currency migration is a required feature, implement an explicit atomic conversion workflow with a recorded rate and audit trail. Owner decision in /plan: (A) block the change once history exists, in AccountForm and the database, or (B) an explicit atomic conversion with a recorded rate and audit trail.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Create an account with history, attempt a currency edit through the UI and API, then edit/delete an old transaction. Verify balances never mix currency units; (b) SQL check inside begin .. rollback (anon, owner and a second user) recorded in the retro; (c) migration applies cleanly to an empty database in CI; (d) the AccountForm hint explains why the currency is locked (if A).

SUMMARY: Pages and heavy features load when they are needed
USER_STORY: As a user on a phone, I want sign-in and Home to open without downloading Reports, charts and import first.
DESCRIPTION: App imports all pages eagerly. The production build reports a 2935.60 kB main JavaScript chunk, 844.40 kB gzip, and warns that chunks exceed 500 kB. The PWA precaches 3525.23 KiB. Impact: Visitors must download and parse report/chart/import features before using login or basic account views. The initial app shell is expensive on slower mobile devices. (REV-024; src/App.tsx:5; src/pages/ReportsPage.tsx:27; vite.config.ts:34). Fix: Lazy-load route pages with React.lazy and useful Suspense boundaries. Load PDF generation, charts and import editors when needed. Adjust service-worker precaching deliberately so deferred features do not all transfer during installation. Measure before choosing extra chunk rules. Measure before adding chunk rules; record before/after build sizes in the retro.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Compare production bundle sizes and cold login/Home loads before and after splitting on a throttled mobile profile. Verify offline navigation for installed features and update behavior; (b) build no longer warns about chunks over 500 kB for the main entry, or the retro states why; (c) installed PWA still opens previously visited pages offline.

SUMMARY: A large offline import is stored in one write
USER_STORY: As a user importing a big file offline, I want the import to save in one step without freezing the app.
DESCRIPTION: Each imported row independently reads/parses the queue, appends one item and writes/stringifies it. Each row also rewrites the account cache and emits notifications. Queue serialization grows approximately quadratically with imported row count. Impact: Large permitted CSV imports can block the main thread, flood subscribers and hit storage limits partway through a save. (REV-025; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:381; src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:164; src/lib/offlineQueue.ts:54). Fix: Add a reusable enqueueMany operation that persists all rows in one transaction. Apply account deltas in one pass, update caches once and emit one notification. Use IndexedDB for larger durable batches.

DESCRIPTION: createClient is called without a generated Database generic. Database row shapes are manually declared and selected data is repeatedly cast to application types. ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Add a type-generation drift check and confirm incorrect column names and RPC arguments fail the build while the pure helper tests remain runnable; (b) type generation drift check in CI; (c) pnpm test still passes.

SUMMARY: Entity reads share one request, cache and error policy
USER_STORY: As a user, I want each account or category list read once per screen and behaving the same offline and on error everywhere.
DESCRIPTION: Each useAccounts instance fetches independently. Layout, payment handling and pages instantiate it together. Similar fetch/cache/offline/error logic is repeated across entity hooks. Only transaction reads currently use dedupeAsync. Impact: The same account query can run several times on mount, and lifecycle fixes must be repeated in many hooks, increasing the chance of inconsistent behavior. (REV-028; src/hooks/useAccounts.ts:21; src/hooks/useCategories.ts:17; src/hooks/useCardPayment.ts:29; src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx:106). Fix: Share entity reads through a user-scoped query store or reusable read hook with request deduplication, key-aware state and consistent offline/error policy. Keep entity-specific business mutations outside the shared read abstraction. Owner decision in /plan: a small in-repo user-scoped query store, or a library (adds a dependency). LED-304, LED-306 and LED-307 build on it.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Mount layout, page and payment hooks together and assert one read per entity/query key. Verify request races, errors and offline behavior through the shared abstraction; (b) unit test for the pure logic in src/lib (deduplication and key-aware state).
